issues.description: Function name mismatch for the |Y> state preparer: the problem statement asks students to implement `_make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (problem_statement.md), while both the template (msd.py) and the reference solution (msd.py) declare and use the function as `make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None` (no leading underscore). This inconsistency means students reading the task text will be told to implement a different identifier than the one present in the starter file and reference solution, and automated tests generated from the problem statement could look for `_make_y_state` and fail to find it.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the function name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fixes (choose one):
1) Update the problem statement to refer to make_y_state(...) (remove the leading underscore) so the task text matches the template and solution; OR
2) Add a thin alias in the template (and reference solution) such as `_make_y_state = make_y_state` so both names are available to students and tests; OR
3) Modify the tests/grader to expect make_y_state instead of `_make_y_state`. Document the chosen canonical name in the task description to avoid future confusion.
